title: Determining Chlorophyll Concentration using CuSO4 Magnesium-Copper Exchange Titration
author: Victor vmr Rodriguez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7xrhpm6
materials: Let the raw mix stand for 00:05:00 minutes.
Write the final results as Con ± Moe

steps.title: Prepare plant‑acetone slurry
steps.instruction: Create a plant‑acetone mixture and filter it to obtain the refined mix.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 g of sample plant material to a mortar.
Add 1 g of magnesium sulfate heptahydrate crystals to the mortar.
Grind until the leaves are pulverized, the magnesium sulfate dissolves, and a liquid forms.
Transfer the solid‑liquid slurry to a 20 mL test tube.
Add 8 mL acetone (Nacalai Tesque Catalog #00310‑95) to the test tube.
Add 1 mL acetone (same catalog) to the mortar, rinse, and collect the wash into the same test tube.
Stir with a glass stirrer, pressing the slurry to the tube base, for 2 minutes; ensure acetone is fully incorporated.
Stir again for 1 minute.
Filter the mixture through a 20 µm retention filtration paper into a new tube (refined mix); use a fresh filter paper for each sample.

steps.title: Generate acid‑activated mix
steps.instruction: Convert the refined mix into an acid‑activated solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL hydrochloric acid to the refined mix and stir with a clean glass stirrer for 1 minute.
Let the acid‑activated mix stand for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare copper(II) sulfate solution
steps.instruction: Make a 60 mg CuSO₄ per mL water solution of copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate (Sigma‑Aldrich Catalog #209198).

steps.title: Set up dilution series
steps.instruction: Create a series of vials with decreasing percentages of acid‑activated mix and complementary acetone.

substeps.instruction: Label ten 5 mL vials in descending order from 100 % to 10 % (10 % resolution).
To each vial, add Acid‑Activated Mix volume = 1000 µL × percentage (decimal).
To each vial, add acetone (Catalog #00310‑95) volume = 1000 µL × (1 − percentage).
Gently stir each vial by rotating in a circular motion for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Transfer to PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Move defined aliquots from the vials into labeled PCR tubes and add copper solution.

substeps.instruction: Using a fresh tip for each transfer, pipette 100 µL of the Acid‑Activated Mix from each vial into a corresponding PCR tube (label tubes with the same percentage).
Add 100 µL copper(II) sulfate solution to each PCR tube.
Seal the tubes and centrifuge at 1200 × g for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Incubate and re‑centrifuge
steps.instruction: Allow reaction to proceed and then re‑centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Place the PCR tubes in a rack and let stand at room temperature for 6 hours.
Centrifuge again at 1200 × g for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Determine endpoint percentages
steps.instruction: Identify the lowest percentage without precipitate (P‑) and the highest percentage with precipitate (P+).

substeps.instruction: Inspect tubes; the lowest‑percentage tube lacking a blue copper(II) sulfate precipitate defines P‑.
The highest‑percentage tube that shows a blue crystalline precipitate defines P+.

steps.title: Calculate concentration and error
steps.instruction: Compute the chlorophyll concentration and its margin of error using the observed endpoints.
